graph_construction: Whole-system provenance graph from OS audit logs (Windows ETW, Linux Audit, CamFlow). Streaming, directed, time-stamped edges from subject (process) to object (process, file, socket); 9 event types; anomaly detection over 15-minute time windows
node_features: Three entity types (process, file, socket). Attributes (path, IP/port) encoded by hierarchical feature hashing into a 16-dimensional vector; each node also has a 100-dimensional state updated over time
edge_features: One-hot event type (9 types) and timestamp
local_mechanism: Temporal graph network (TGN) encoder using a UniMP GNN over a sampled neighborhood of 20 nodes, GRU node-state update, MLP decoder that reconstructs the edge type (reconstruction error is the anomaly signal)
split_protocol: Within-dataset, split by time. Trained on benign data only; Manzoor: 1 graph train, 24 validation, 75 benign and 100 attack graphs test; DARPA: benign days for training and validation, attack days for test (Table 12)
ood_evaluation: none (no cross-dataset or cross-system test). Concept drift is shown on E5-ClearScope by retraining on false-positive data (Sec. 5.2); an evasion dataset is tested in Sec. 6
metrics: Precision, recall, accuracy and AUC per time window (TP, TN, FP, FN counts); node-level and graph-level protocols when comparing with ThreaTrace and Unicorn; also attack-summary graph size, run time, CPU and memory
tuning_fairness: not reported (Kairos hyperparameters chosen by a sensitivity study on the test datasets, Sec. 5.4; baseline tuning is not described)
notes: Baselines are Unicorn and ThreaTrace only; ProvDetector re-implementation failed and ShadeWatcher is not fully open source (Sec. 5.3). Unicorn skipped on E5 because it would need extensive tuning. Adjusted results (Table 5) come from the authors manually re-labeling false positives. Authors list evaluation limitations in Sec. 6. Code: github.com/ProvenanceAnalytics/kairos

graph_construction: System logs (Windows Event Logs, Linux Audit Logs) cut into batches of K events (250k in experiments), each batch turned into a provenance graph. Nodes = processes plus objects (files, network flows, modules); edges = system calls. GraphSAGE runs on the graph after selective traversal rules (TP1-TP4) that drop duplicate, low-priority and execution-specific edges
node_features: Word2Vec embedding of a "summary sentence" per node: its attributes (process name and command line, file path, IP and port, module name) plus the event types to its 1-hop neighbors, sorted by timestamp, with positional encoding, then averaged. GNN embedding is concatenated with this for XGBoost
edge_features: Event type (syscall) and timestamp. Used to build the node sentences and to filter edges; no learned edge features
local_mechanism: GraphSAGE (SAGEConv) trained to predict node type (process, file, socket) with weighted cross-entropy. XGBoost classifier on concatenated Word2Vec + GNN embeddings. Anomaly = predicted type differs from true type, above a confidence threshold
global_mechanism: none Only k-hop neighborhood aggregation. No attention or Transformer
positional_encoding: Sinusoidal positional encoding (from Vaswani) added to word embeddings in the node sentence to keep event order. It is not a graph positional encoding
datasets: DARPA E3 (Cadets, Trace, Theia, FiveDirections), DARPA OpTC (attacks 1-3), StreamSpot, Unicorn (SC-1, SC-2)
split_protocol: OpTC: 6 benign days for training, next 3 attack days for testing; benign data split into initial training and fine-tuning, plus a benign validation set to set the threshold. E3 labels taken from ThreaTrace; OpTC labels from DARPA ground truth. StreamSpot and Unicorn use their own splits. Jaccard threshold 1
ood_evaluation: none. Only a mimicry attack (Goyal et al.) was tested, and training with 10 hosts vs more. No unseen-network or size-shift test
metrics: Precision, recall, F-score, TP/FP/FN/TN, ROC-AUC, CDF of alert scores; also inference and training time, RAM, CPU
tuning_fairness: not reported. Compared only with ThreaTrace (run by the authors on OpTC) and Unicorn (only on Unicorn's own datasets because of its many hyperparameters). ShadeWatcher and ProGrapher were skipped (closed source). No baseline tuning described
notes: Proposes FLASH, a host provenance IDS using GraphSAGE GNNs and Word2Vec on OS audit logs (DARPA E3, OpTC). Introduces an embedding recycling database that reuses pre-computed GNN node embeddings, achieving real-time node-level anomaly detection with up to 3× speedup.

graph_construction: NetFlow records as a graph; nodes = (IP, port) endpoints; edges = flows
node_features: None: all nodes get a vector of all 1s (featureless)
edge_features: NetFlow fields (packet and byte counts, flow duration, etc.)
global_mechanism: Transformer Encoder (multi-head self-attention for global context)
metrics: Accuracy, precision, recall, F1, false alarm rate; binary and multi-class weighted F1
notes: Proposes a hybrid network intrusion detector combining Graph Neural Networks and Transformer architectures. Evaluates network flow computational graphs to capture both local structural topology and global long-range contextual relationships.

graph_construction: Fixed-duration (15 min) provenance snapshots; each of the 8 evaluated PIDS builds its own graph
node_features: Text embeddings of paths, commands and IPs (Word2Vec, FastText, HFH, Doc2Vec), or node type only
local_mechanism: Evaluated: GraphSAGE, GAT, TGN, Graph-LSTM, VAE-based (NodLink); proposed Velox: linear layers with no GNN
datasets: DARPA E3 (CADETS, THEIA, CLEARSCOPE), E5 (same three), OpTC (H201, H501, H051)
split_protocol: Train on benign days, one validation day, test on attack days (Bilot Tables 7-9); no data snooping
metrics: ADP (their new metric), precision, TP and FP counts, relative std of ADP
tuning_fairness: Yes: every system tuned, including baselines (SC4)
notes: Empirical benchmark evaluating 8 leading provenance IDSs(7 featuring GNN/graph architectures) on OS audit logs. Introduces a lightweight linear baseline (VELOX), demonstrating that simpler non-graph models can SOTA GNN performance on standard datasets.

graph_construction: Linux Audit records (32 syscall types) or DARPA CDM records parsed offline into one provenance graph per dataset; nodes = processes, files, sockets; edges = syscalls with timestamps. Noise reduction (causality-preserving reduction, temporary-file and library removal) cuts about 95% of TRACE edges (App. B). The graph is split into behaviors (subgraphs rooted at data objects, found by forward DFS, from Watson); entity pairs inside a behavior form a bipartite interaction graph, which is merged with the provenance graph into a knowledge graph with syscall relations plus an 'interact' relation (Sec. V). Not streaming (App. A)
node_features: No attribute features. Each entity gets a learned TransR embedding (entity size 32) trained on knowledge-graph triples; attributes (pid, exe, args, file name and path, IP and port) only identify entities. New entities need retraining (App. A)
edge_features: Relation type (syscall type, or 'interact'); each relation has its own TransR embedding and projection matrix. Timestamps are stored on provenance edges but not used by the model
local_mechanism: KGAT-style GNN: attentive propagation (attention from TransR embeddings, softmax over neighbors), GraphSAGE concatenation aggregator with LeakyReLU, 2 layers (32 and 16), layer outputs concatenated; the inner product of two entity vectors scores an interaction. Trained with the TransR margin loss plus a BPR pairwise loss on observed (benign) interactions vs randomly sampled unobserved ones (Sec. VI)
datasets: DARPA-E3-TRACE (4 attacks: Extension Backdoor, Firefox Backdoor, Pine Backdoor, Phishing Executable); Simulated dataset (6 attacks from earlier papers re-run in the authors' testbed: Configuration Leakage, Content Destruction, Cheating Student, Illegal Storage, Passwd Gzip Scp, Passwd Reuse)
split_protocol: Within-dataset random split of system entity interactions: 80% train, 10% validation, 10% test, disjoint; hyperparameters tuned on validation only (Sec. VIII-A). Training uses benign interactions plus randomly sampled unobserved interactions (2 per benign one, App. C). Ground truth labeled by hand by the authors. The model-adaption test instead orders interactions by time: first 80% (or 90%) train, last 10% test (Sec. VIII-D)
ood_evaluation: none (no cross-dataset, cross-host or later-time test). Retraining on analyst-labeled false positives (Sec. VIII-D), training-data contamination (Sec. IX) and detection from pre-privilege-escalation data only (App. G) are tested
metrics: Precision, recall, F1, accuracy and TP/TN/FP/FN at the interaction level (pairs of entities); false positive rate on benign test interactions; AUC and ROC curves; runtime, throughput, CPU and memory
tuning_fairness: none (no baseline detector is run). Only ablations on TRACE: TransR alone and one-hot, TransE or TransH plus GNN (Fig. 6). Poirot, Morse and Unicorn are compared in text only (Sec. VIII-C). ShadeWatcher tuned by grid search on validation (learning rate, embedding size, layers, threshold)
seeds: not reported (runtime is averaged over 5 runs, Table VI)
notes: Code: github.com/jun-zeng/ShadeWatcher. Open PDF: jun-zeng.github.io/file/shadewatcher_paper.pdf. With a random interaction-level split, the paper does not say how attack interactions are kept out of training (verify). Final settings: learning rate 0.001, embedding 32, 2 layers, threshold -0.5, 30 epochs with early stopping, dropout 0.2 (Sec. VII). Reported FPR: 0.332% TRACE, 0.137% Simulated (Table IV).

graph_construction: One software installation graph (SIG) per installation. Windows ETW (enterprise) or Linux Audit (testbed) events become edges from subject to object; built by backtracking from the installed executable(s) to the installer download, with a time bound on generic system services; several backtraces are merged. Made acyclic by node versioning. Each SIG is a bounded, static DAG analyzed as a whole (Sec. 4.2)
node_features: Word2vec skip-gram embeddings of file-system path components (128 dimensions, window 5, 10 directed random walks of length 10); a node vector is the normalized sum of its path-component embeddings. Unseen nodes embedded with a la carte (Sec. 4.3, 5.2)
edge_features: Edge type only (process start, end; file rename, read, write, execute, delete; socket send, receive, Table 1); the graph LSTM treats edge types separately. No timestamps beyond DAG order
local_mechanism: Autoencoder: graph LSTM encoder (Peng et al.) over the DAG, where each process node's hidden state comes from its embedding and the hidden states of all its source nodes, by edge type; MLP decoder reconstructs the node embedding. Each process node's reconstruction loss is its anomaly score; a graph is flagged when its Jenks natural-breaks max-zone average loss exceeds the mean + 3 std over validation graphs (Sec. 4.4-4.5, Alg. 1)
global_mechanism: none (no attention). The graph LSTM passes state along DAG paths, so a node is informed by all its ancestors, not only 1 hop
datasets: NEC Labs America enterprise Windows ETW data (141 machines, 20 software installers, Table 2); 625 malicious installers (6 found in the wild, Table 3, the rest built by the authors by bundling or embedding 20 VirusShare malware samples into benign installers, Table 4); Linux testbed with 2,885 Python package installation graphs and the malicious python3-dateutil PyPI package (Sec. 5.12)
split_protocol: Per installer: benign SIGs split 70% train, 10% validation (sets the threshold), 20% benign test (Sec. 5.2). Trained on benign data only; malicious installers appear only in the test set. Linux: 1,708 benign graphs for training, 1,176 benign graphs of other packages for testing
ood_evaluation: yes. (1) Adjacent software version: a model trained on one version is tested on 1 benign and 1 malicious install of the next or previous version (Sec. 5.6, Table 7). (2) Meta-model trained without Skype and tested on Skype; then with 5-40% of applications held out and tested on them (Sec. 5.10, Fig. 9). (3) Linux model tested on benign packages not seen in training (Sec. 5.12). Also training contamination of 5-25% (Sec. 5.8) and black-box adversarial attacks (Sec. 5.9)
metrics: Precision, recall, accuracy, F-score and FP percentage at the graph (installation) level; AUC (contamination, adversarial and meta-model tests); FPR on Linux; process-level attribution as top-5 or top-10 ranks within k hops of the malware process (basic, improved and targeted guidance, Fig. 3). The commercial TDS is scored per event
tuning_fairness: not reported. StreamSpot and Frappuccino run with the setups from their papers or public code; StreamSpot reimplemented by the authors to look at larger neighborhoods (Sec. 5.4). No tuning budget described for SIGL or the baselines; SIGL settings fixed, best epoch chosen on validation
notes: Open PDF: usenix.org/system/files/sec21-han-xueyuan.pdf (also arXiv 2008.11533). Split is given as 80/20 train/validation in Sec. 4.1 but 70/10/20 in Sec. 5.2 (verify). Detection is per installation with one model per application (or a meta-model), not continuous whole-system monitoring. Most malicious installers are synthetic, made by the authors. Baselines: commercial TDS (NEC ASI), StreamSpot, Frappuccino (Table 5). 100 epochs, batch 25, PyTorch and DGL.

graph_construction: Whole-system provenance graphs from OS audit logs. Nodes = processes, files, sockets, IPC; edges = system calls. StreamSpot uses 600 scenario graphs; DARPA TC THEIA splits one large graph into 25 temporal subgraphs. Detectors decompose graphs via K-hop chunks (StreamSpot, Unicorn), paths (ProvDetector, Pagoda), or full graphs (FGA).
node_features: FGA: not reported. StreamSpot: coarse entity types (file, process). Unicorn: node labels in histograms. ProvDetector: doc2vec path text embeddings.
edge_features: System event types (calls). FGA: not reported.
local_mechanism: Evaluates 5 detectors; FGA (authors' SIGL-like proxy) is the only GNN: PyTorch Geometric GCN node encoder with inner-product neighborhood reconstruction decoder trained on benign data. Non-GNNs: StreamSpot (StreamHash), Unicorn (HistoSketch), ProvDetector (doc2vec + LOF), Pagoda (path rarity).
datasets: StreamSpot (5 benign + 1 drive-by attack scenario x 100 runs) and DARPA TC3 THEIA (Drakon backdoor attack).
split_protocol: StreamSpot: trained on benign CNN browsing scenario, evaluated on 100 attack graphs before and after mimicry edits. FGA threshold set on benign validation set.
ood_evaluation: none (no cross-dataset or size-shift test; evaluates adversarial robustness via 3 mimicry gadgets).
metrics: Graph-level: evasion success rate (100% across all 5 detectors), distance to benign clusters vs added edges, baseline TPR/TNR, and step runtimes.
tuning_fairness: not reported. Public defaults used for StreamSpot/Unicorn; ProvDetector/Pagoda reimplemented; FGA untuned.
notes: Attack paper included for FGA (GCN autoencoder). Shows whole-graph provenance detectors reach 100% evasion under adversarial mimicry shift despite near-perfect in-distribution TPR/TNR.

graph_construction: Discrete-time snapshot sequence (30-min window) from LANL 2015 auth logs (auth.txt). Nodes = entities (users, computers, DCs); directed edges = authentications in window merged into weighted links. Snapshots distributed across workers for parallel GNN encoding.
node_features: One-hot node ID concatenated with a one-hot type vector (user, computer, special administrative machine).
edge_features: Single weight equal to the sigmoid of standardized authentication count within time window; no edge types.
local_mechanism: 2-layer GCN (32-d) per snapshot with edge dropout, tanh, then GRU (32-d) across time to MLP (16-d). Inner-product decoder predicts edge likelihoods trained with BCE loss on benign edges vs sampled non-edges. Modes: link detection (inductive) and link prediction (transductive).
global_mechanism: none (RNN operates across time, not graph nodes).
datasets: LANL 2015 Cyber Events (58 days, 17,685 nodes, 518 attack edges); Facebook, Enron10, COLAB benchmarks.
split_protocol: LANL: within-dataset temporal split. Trains on all snapshots prior to first attack edge (last 5% tunes threshold; 5% edges/snapshot masked for validation). Test set = all subsequent attack snapshots.
ood_evaluation: none (single network; varies snapshot window delta).
metrics: Edge-level: AUC, AP, TPR, FPR, Precision (GCN+GRU best: AUC 0.9912, AP 0.0523, TPR 86.10%, FPR 0.57%). Also measures distributed speedup.
tuning_fairness: not reported. LR grid search on benchmarks {0.03, 0.02, 0.01, 0.005}; baseline metrics taken from prior literature or re-run where scalable.
notes: Primary contribution is parallel snapshot encoding for near-linear training speedup. The authors acknowledge that a 0.57% FPR remains too high for standalone SOC deployment and note coarse ground-truth labeling in LANL.
